scope: Public-data-only explanatory-depth summary before Chapter 3; restricted Taiwan palaeoclimate is a descendant-lineage sensitivity after cross-study chronology refinement.

orientation.calendar_constraint: cross-study core-Nipponocirsium stem after C. morii and before Japanese-Taiwan core split; central estimates 0.79-0.74 Ma are not a joint interval

dated_local_events: C. brevicaule C->W, 0-0.93 Ma terminal envelope
C. kawakamii C->W, 0-0.47 Ma topology-union terminal envelope
flower_colour.historical_driver_status: not directly evaluable because no commensurate surface-RSDS history and population colour is not lineage-fixed

restricted_taiwan_orientation_sensitivit.status: not the unique origin-event environment after Japanese-core taxon addition

BIO12.interpretation: positive and compatible with Azami direction, but typical

BIO15.interpretation: decrease, opposite present D-high niche; paleolocation signs mixed

anthesis_precipitation.decision: directionally compatible rainfall increase across all Taiwan cells, but not exceptional versus same-duration windows; current descendant flowering months are not ancestral phenology

sea_level.decision: not an unusually volatile global sea-level interval; no local land-bridge claim

process_model_status.ST1_persistent_driver: not supported by the restricted Taiwan test and not evaluable for the refined origin branch because paleolocation is unresolved
process_model_status.ST3_driver_switching_selection_mosaic: plausible but requires multiple dated, located events

public_data_ceiling: Public data resolve recurrence and relative depth broadly, local calendar constraints for selected events, and present-space ecological correspondence. They do not yet jointly identify the exact origin location, event-specific selective pressure, mechanism, or fitness effect.
chapter3_handoff: Use ancestry-linked population samples to calibrate phenotype, actual flowering-season exposure, mechanism/mediator and reproductive fitness; prioritize orientation-hydric and colour-radiation hypotheses while explicitly testing origin-maintenance decoupling.
